standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's answer and the pages it got: the Anker SOLIX F3800 / F3800 Plus product pages, the F3800 Plus Technical Brief (Salesforce and THD copies), the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus manual and the jackery.com Solar Generator 5000 Plus pages. They all cover Anker or Jackery hardware. None covers the BLUETTI Apex 300, the only 240 V unit whose kit with panels I could verify as in stock in an approved store today (Anker's F3800 Plus page shows Sold Out with no price). ChatGPT's answer does say that 'a 240V outlet's rated amperage does not guarantee the generator can deliver that full power', so the general warning is already there and only the numbers are new (3,840 W = 16 A at 240 V on a 50 A outlet). The solar-input voltage limit and the one-panel-per-input wiring rule are new. They decide how many panels go in the kit and how long a refill takes.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh LFP, 3,840 W, one 120/240 V NEMA 14-50R outlet). A single unit gives 240 V. The 240 V load must stay at or below 16 A (3,840 W ÷ 240 V).

Solar panels: 2 × BLUETTI 500 W (SORA 500). The Voc of 49.1 V is under the Apex 300's 60 V input limit, so each panel goes on its own input. Two panels in series (98.2 V) exceed the limit, and two in parallel (Isc 2 × 13.31 = 26.6 A) exceed the 20 A per-input limit, so two panels is the most this unit can use.

Optional capacity: BLUETTI B300K expansion battery (2,764.8 Wh). The bundle with two 500 W panels doubles the energy on the same 1,000 W of solar, so a full refill takes twice as long (5,529.6 Wh ÷ 800 W ≈ 6.9 h of full sun).
Optional: BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable (MC4, 30 A, 5 m / 10 m) to place the panels farther from the unit. The listing says to use one cable set per panel.

findings.label: AC output, rated (all outlets, 120/240 V)
findings.note: BLUETTI's figure as printed in StorageReview's spec table. I could not open the maker page (redirect loop) or the US manual (PDF over the fetch size limit). At 240 V: 3,840 W ÷ 240 V = 16 A available.

findings.label: 240 V outlet
findings.note: The outlet is rated 50 A, but the unit supplies 16 A at 240 V (3,840 ÷ 240), which is 32% of the outlet rating. A 240 V load drawing more than 16 A running will not run from it.

findings.label: Solar input
findings.value: 2 inputs, each 12–60 V DC, 20 A, 1,200 W (2,400 W total)
findings.note: BLUETTI's figures from the reviewer's spec table. The manual's line 'do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V' appeared only in a search snippet, because the manual PDF could not be opened.

findings.label: Measured usable energy (single unit, full discharge)
findings.note: Measured by StorageReview. Runtime at the full 3,840 W: 2,390 ÷ 3,840 = 0.62 h, about 37 min. At 1,500 W: 2,390 ÷ 1,500 = 1.6 h. With two B300K packs StorageReview measured 7.38 kWh (89%).

findings.label: Measured recharge energy (AC) and round trip
findings.value: 3.30 kWh in to refill; about 72% round trip
findings.note: Measured on AC charging, so it does not carry over directly to solar (DC) charging. It still shows that refilling takes more energy than the rated capacity.

Arithmetic against the Apex 300 input limits: 2 in series = 98.2 V Voc > 60 V (not allowed); 2 in parallel = 26.6 A Isc > 20 A (over the limit); so one panel per input and two panels per Apex 300.
